properties.name: McMurdo Station, Ross Island
properties.subtitle: Ross Dependency, Antarctica
properties.claim: The scale of the US Antarctic Program — an airfield, a former nuclear reactor, continuous military airlift and high-profile visitors — is presented as cover for work at a site under the ice.
properties.context: McMurdo is the logistics hub for US Antarctic science, and its operations are published in annual USAP reports with open science plans. The PM-3A reactor operated 1962–72 and was removed; its decommissioning is documented. The research it supports is likewise public: the IceCube neutrino observatory at the Pole, ice-core palaeoclimate programmes, and the Antarctic meteorite collection that yielded the Martian meteorite ALH84001.
properties.summary: McMurdo Station is an American Antarctic research station on the southern tip of Ross Island. It is operated by the United States through the United States Antarctic Program (USAP), a branch of the National Science Foundation (NSF). The station is the largest community in Antarctica, capable of supporting up to 1,200 residents, though the population fluctuates seasonally; during the Antarctic night, there are fewer than two hundred people.
